mainTopic: Gaps between the סכך and the walls (לבוד and דופן עקומה), why the משנה lists several cases, and רבה's debate with בי רב over the measures for אויר and סכך פסול
overview: The משנה gives three rulings about gaps between the סכך and the walls. If the סכך is pulled three טפחים away from the walls, the סוכה is פסולה. If four אמות of פסול covering separate the wall from the סכך, the סוכה is also פסולה. This applies to a breached house roof, a courtyard with an אכסדרה, and a large סוכה edged with פסול material. Less than four אמות is fine because of דופן עקומה. The גמרא explains with a צריכא why each of the three cases teaches something new. רבה then reports that the חכמים of בי רב say אויר ruins a סוכה at three טפחים and סכך פסול at four טפחים. רבה challenges them from the house case, and they answer that it is about דופן עקומה. The two sides then trade a puzzle about filling an air gap with skewers. רבה begins his reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Roofing pulled three handbreadths away from the walls
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the סכך is kept three טפחים away from the walls, the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone placed the roofing three handbreadths away from the walls, the סוכה is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a simple case. The סכך does not reach the walls, and there is a gap of three טפחים of open air between them, so the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of less than three טפחים does not matter, because of the rule of לבוד: the gap is treated as if it were closed. Once the gap reaches three טפחים, לבוד no longer works. The walls and the סכך are then no longer joined into one סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core text being studied)
He distanced, placed far away
The act of roofing, or the roofing itself (סכך)
Walls of the סוכה
Handbreadths (a unit of measure)
Unfit, invalid

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one distanced the roofing
from the walls by three handbreadths
it is unfit.
phrases.notes: A gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed; that's the rule of לבוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִרְחִיק אֶת הַסִּיכּוּךְ מִן הַדְּפָנוֹת שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of three טפחים of open air between the סכך and the walls makes the סוכה פסולה.

steps.title: A house with a hole in its roof
steps.stepSummary: A house's roof has a hole that is covered with סכך. If four אמות of the old roof separate the wall from the סכך, the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house whose roof was broken open, and someone placed roofing over the hole: if there are four cubits from the wall to the roofing, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now discusses a different kind of gap. This time the gap is filled with the old, פסול house roof rather than open air, and the משנה says four אמות of it makes the סוכה פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than four אמות of old roof is fine, because of the rule of דופן עקומה, the bent wall. We picture the wall as bending over and running along the ceiling until it reaches the סכך. That picture only works up to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Was breached or broken open (a hole was made)
He put on סכך, roofed it
Wall
Cubits (a larger measure, about six טפחים each)
Bent wall: the idea that the wall continues along the ceiling

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measurements. Three טפחים applies to empty air (לבוד). Four אמות applies to פסול roofing (דופן עקומה). They are different rules for different kinds of gaps.

phrases.english: A house that was breached
and one placed roofing over it
if there is, from the wall to the roofing,
four cubits, it is unfit.
phrases.notes: Under four אמות it's still כשרה, because of the rule of דופן עקומה, the 'bent wall'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a gap of open air to a gap of פסול roofing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four אמות of פסול roof between the wall and the סכך makes the סוכה פסולה. Less than that is כשרה because of דופן עקומה.

steps.title: A courtyard with a portico, and a large סוכה edged with invalid roofing
steps.stepSummary: The same four-אמות rule applies to a courtyard surrounded by an אכסדרה and to a large סוכה whose edges are covered with material that may not be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a courtyard surrounded by a portico, and a large סוכה that was surrounded with material that may not be used for roofing: if there are four cubits beneath it, the סוכה is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more cases that follow the same rule. If four אמות of פסול covering stand between the wall and the כשר סכך, the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the roof of the אכסדרה plays the part of the old house roof. In the second case, פסול material placed around the edge plays that part. Under four אמות, דופן עקומה still saves the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard
Surrounded
Portico: a roofed area without full walls
Something that may not be used as סכך
Underneath it

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases in the second half of the משנה share one rule: פסול covering next to the wall is acceptable under four אמות and פסול at four אמות or more.

phrases.english: And likewise, a courtyard that is surrounded by a portico
and a large sukkah that was surrounded
with material that one may not use for roofing
if there are four cubits beneath it
it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same four-אמות rule to two more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four אמות of פסול covering, whether an אכסדרה roof or פסול material, makes the סוכה פסולה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list all these cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs several cases that all teach the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need all these cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the house, the courtyard and the large סוכה all teach the same idea. It asks why the משנה needs all of them, and this question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that the משנה does not waste words. If one case would be enough, each extra case must be teaching something new. The גמרא is asking what that new lesson is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why do I need all these?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need all these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה repeats the same rule in several cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each extra case in the משנה teaches that the others do not.

steps.title: The courtyard case is needed because its walls were not built for the portico
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a צריכא. From the house case alone, we might think דופן עקומה works only when the walls were built for that roof. The courtyard case teaches that it works even when the walls were not built for the אכסדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. For if the משנה had taught us only the breached house, we would say the rule applies there because those walls were made for the house. But in a courtyard surrounded by a portico, whose walls were not made for the portico, I would say the rule does not apply. So it is necessary to teach it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needs the courtyard case in addition to the house case. The next step explains what the large-סוכה case adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house case, the walls and the roof belong together, so it is easy to picture the wall bending along the roof. In the courtyard, the walls belong to the house and only happen to border the אכסדרה. We might think דופן עקומה does not apply there, so the משנה teaches that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: each case teaches something unique
It taught us
Walls, partitions
Were made for
I would have said no

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that דופן עקומה does not depend on why the walls were built. A wall that was built for some other purpose can still bend to join the סכך.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying "אֵימָא לָא" is not the conclusion. It is only what we might have wrongly thought without the courtyard case. The actual law is that the courtyard follows the same rule.

phrases.english: It is necessary:
for if it had taught us only the breached house,
I would say it applies there because those walls were made for the house.
But a courtyard surrounded by a portico,
whose walls were not made for the portico,
I would say the rule does not apply;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the משנה lists several cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The house case alone could suggest that דופן עקומה requires walls built for that roof. The courtyard case shows it applies even to walls that were not built for the אכסדרה.

steps.title: Why the large-סוכה case is also needed
steps.stepSummary: The צריכא concludes. The house and courtyard cases alone would not teach that דופן עקומה works when the edges are covered with real סכך פסול, so the large-סוכה case is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had only taught these two cases (the house and the courtyard), I would say דופן עקומה works there because their roof material is itself valid סכך material. But in a large סוכה surrounded with material that may not be used as סכך, the roofing really is invalid סכך, so I might say דופן עקומה does not work. That is why this case is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer about why the משנה needed all three cases. It explains what the third case, the large סוכה, adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house and the courtyard, the old roof is made of valid material. It is only invalid because it was not put up for the sake of the סוכה. In the large סוכה, the edge is covered with material that is invalid by its very nature. We might have thought דופן עקומה cannot stretch across that kind of material, so the משנה teaches that it can.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us
These two (cases)
Valid roofing material
A large סוכה
It is necessary (each case teaches something new)

steps.whatToRemember: The three cases build on each other. The house case teaches that דופן עקומה works with walls built for that roof. The courtyard case shows it works even when the walls were not built for the אכסדרה. The large-סוכה case shows it works even across material that is invalid by nature.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only these two cases,
(I would say it works) because their roofing is valid roofing material,
phrases.notes: The old roof of the house or אכסדרה is valid material. It is only invalid because it was not made for the סוכה.

phrases.english: but a large sukkah
whose edges were surrounded with material that may not be used for roofing,
where its roofing is truly invalid roofing,
I would say no (it does not work). So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in step 5 by explaining what the third case adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The large-סוכה case teaches that דופן עקומה works even when the material in between is invalid by its very nature, not only when it is valid material that was not made for the סוכה.

steps.title: The Sages of רב's academy: air at three, invalid roofing at four
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports that the חכמים of בי רב said that אויר ruins a סוכה at three טפחים, while סכך פסול ruins it at four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I found the חכמים of the house of רב sitting and saying: empty air disqualifies at three טפחים, and invalid roofing disqualifies at four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבה quotes a rule about the measures of empty air and of invalid roofing, which sets up the debate in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different measures here. A gap of empty air inside the סוכה ruins it at only three טפחים. A strip of invalid roofing is treated more leniently and ruins it only at four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of רב's academy
Empty air (a gap with no roofing)
Invalid roofing material
Disqualifies

steps.confusionAlert: Here "four" means four טפחים (handbreadths), not four אמות. Do not mix this up with the four אמות in the משנה's house case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two basic measures for problems in the middle of the סכך: three טפחים for air and four טפחים for סכך פסול.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
I found the Sages of the house of Rav
who were sitting and saying:
Empty air disqualifies at three (handbreadths),
invalid roofing disqualifies at four (handbreadths).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, though it uses the same משנה about three טפחים and four אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Empty air ruins a סוכה at three טפחים. סכך פסול ruins it at four טפחים.

steps.title: רבה's challenge: then סכך פסול should need four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges them. If the three-טפחים rule for air comes from our משנה, then the same משנה's house case should teach that סכך פסול only ruins a סוכה at four אמות, not four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to them: Where do you learn that air disqualifies at three? From the משנה, which says that if one kept the סכך three טפחים away from the walls, the סוכה is invalid. If so, invalid roofing should also only disqualify at four אמות. The same משנה says: a house that was breached and covered with סכך, if there are four אמות between the סכך and the wall, the סוכה is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the rule of the חכמים of בי רב. He argues that their own source would force a much bigger measure for סכך פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה assumes the חכמים learn "three for air" from the first case of the משנה. But the very same משנה, in the house case, seems to say that invalid roofing (the old roof) only ruins the סוכה at four אמות. So if they read the משנה this way, they should say four אמות for סכך פסול, not four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know it?
He distanced (kept away)
A house whose roof was breached
Four cubits

phrases.english: And I said to them:
That air disqualifies at three, from where do you know it?
It is as we learned:
If one kept the roofing away from the walls
three handbreadths, it is invalid.
Then invalid roofing too
should disqualify only at four cubits,
as we learned:
A house that was breached, and one put roofing over it,
if there is between the roofing and the wall
four cubits, it is invalid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ אֲנָא: אֲוִיר דְּפוֹסֵל בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְנָא לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the four-טפחים measure for סכך פסול given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that סכך פסול disqualifies at four טפחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה that gives three טפחים for air gives four אמות in the house case. So consistency demands four אמות for סכך פסול.

steps.title: The house case is about the bent wall, not a roofing measure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the house case is not a source for any measure of סכך פסול. As רב and שמואל both say, it is based on דופן עקומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to me: Leave that case aside, because רב and שמואל both say that the משנה there was dealing with דופן עקומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים of בי רב answer רבה's challenge. They explain that the house case has nothing to do with how much invalid roofing ruins a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house case, the old roof is not judged as סכך פסול in the middle of the סוכה. Instead we view it as part of the wall, bent over. That works up to four אמות, which is why four אמות appears there. So the four-טפחים measure for סכך פסול is not contradicted by that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Apart from that one (leave that case aside)
Both of them
A bent wall (invalid roof treated as part of the wall)
They dealt with it (that principle)

steps.whatToRemember: Four אמות is the limit of דופן עקומה, an extension of the wall. Four טפחים is the measure for סכך פסול in the middle of the סוכה. These are two different rules.

phrases.english: And they said to me:
Leave that case aside,
for Rav and Shmuel both say:
The Sages there dealt with the principle of the bent wall.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the challenging case is based on a different principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four אמות in the house case is the measure at which סכך פסול ruins a סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four אמות is the limit of דופן עקומה, not a measure of סכך פסול. So the four-טפחים rule stands.

steps.title: רבה's skewers paradox against the four-טפחים rule
steps.stepSummary: רבה points out a strange result of the four-טפחים rule. A סוכה with less than four טפחים of סכך פסול next to less than three טפחים of air is כשרה. But if the air is filled with unfit skewers, it becomes פסולה. Air is supposed to be the stricter thing, since it ruins at only three, so this makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: Suppose a סוכה has less than four טפחים of סכך פסול and, next to it, less than three טפחים of open air. What is its status? It is כשרה. Now suppose someone fills the air with skewers. What is its status? It is פסולה. But shouldn't air, which ruins a סוכה at only three, be at least as strict as סכך פסול, which ruins only at four?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is still reporting what he said to the חכמים of בי רב. He builds a test case to show that their four-טפחים rule produces a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each gap alone is under its limit, so the סוכה is כשרה. Filling the air with skewers, which are סכך פסול, can push the total סכך פסול to four טפחים or more, so the סוכה becomes פסולה. That means covering a hole with something actually made things worse, even though air is treated as the stricter problem, since it ruins at three. That contradiction is רבה's attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Skewers (metal spits). They are not valid סכך, so they count as סכך פסול.
Open air: a gap with no roofing at all.
Unfit roofing: material that may not serve as סכך.
He filled it (here, he filled the air gap).
Valid / invalid (said of the סוכה).

steps.confusionAlert: Air is the 'stricter' thing here because it ruins a סוכה at a smaller size, three טפחים instead of four. So it seems backwards that the סוכה is fine with air but ruined once that air is replaced by סכך פסול.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
phrases.notes: רבה is speaking, still reporting his debate with the חכמים of בי רב.

phrases.english: What if there is unfit roofing
less than four (handbreadths)
phrases.notes: Just under the limit for סכך פסול according to the חכמים.

phrases.english: and air less than three (handbreadths), what is its status?
phrases.notes: Just under the limit for air.

phrases.english: It is valid.
phrases.notes: Neither gap reaches its own limit.

phrases.english: If he filled it (the air) with skewers, what then?
It is invalid,
phrases.notes: The total סכך פסול now reaches four טפחים.

phrases.english: but should air, which invalidates at three, not be
(at least) like unfit roofing, which invalidates at four?!
phrases.notes: This is a challenge: that result just doesn't make sense.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ אֲנָא: מָה אִילּוּ אִיכָּא סְכָךְ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חכמים answered his first challenge in Step 9, רבה attacks their four-טפחים rule a second way, by showing that it leads to an absurd result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's rule that סכך פסול ruins a סוכה at four טפחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that rule, replacing harmless air with skewers turns a valid סוכה into an invalid one. That treats air (limit of three) more leniently than סכך פסול (limit of four), which is backwards.

steps.title: The חכמים show the same paradox applies to רבה's four-אמות view
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that רבה's own view, that סכך פסול ruins a סוכה only at four אמות, has the exact same problem. Less than four אמות of סכך פסול plus less than three טפחים of air is כשרה, yet filling the air with skewers makes it פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they said to me: If so, the same problem hits you too, since you say סכך פסול ruins a סוכה at four אמות. Suppose there is less than four אמות of סכך פסול and less than three טפחים of air. What is its status? It is כשרה. If he fills the air with skewers, what then? It is פסולה. So shouldn't air, which ruins at three, be like סכך פסול, which ruins at four אמות?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים do not answer רבה's question directly. Instead, they show that the same strange result happens under רבה's own opinion, so his challenge cannot be used against them alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same as before, with four אמות in place of four טפחים. If the סכך פסול is just under four אמות, adding skewers in the air gap can push it to four אמות, so the סוכה becomes פסולה. Since the paradox exists in both views, the חכמים argue it does not disprove their view in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces the claim that the argument leads to a problem.
According to you too: the same difficulty applies to your view.
Four אמות: רבה's measure for when סכך פסול ruins a סוכה.

phrases.english: And they said to me: If so,
phrases.notes: The חכמים of בי רב are responding.

phrases.english: according to you too,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרַתְּ סְכָךְ פָּסוּל פּוֹסֵל בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: who said that unfit roofing invalidates at four cubits,
phrases.notes: רבה's position, derived from the house case in the משנה.

phrases.english: what if there is unfit roofing
less than four cubits
and air less than three (handbreadths), what is its status?
It is valid.
If he filled it with skewers, what then?
It is invalid.
phrases.notes: The סכך פסול now reaches four אמות.

phrases.english: Should air, which invalidates at three, not be
like unfit roofing, which invalidates at four cubits?!
phrases.notes: The same paradox, now aimed at רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרוּ לִי: אִי הָכִי, לְדִידָךְ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רבה's challenge in Step 10 by turning the identical argument back against his own view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the idea that the skewers paradox disproves the four-טפחים rule specifically.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The paradox is not unique to the חכמים. It arises equally under רבה's four-אמות view, so it cannot decide between them.

steps.title: רבה begins explaining why his view avoids the paradox
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the comparison and starts to explain that under his four-אמות view the problem does not arise. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: What is this comparison? It works well according to me, since I say four אמות...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins his reply to the חכמים' counter-argument. This line sets up his explanation, which is completed in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the words 'הַאי מַאי', רבה claims the two cases are not really alike. 'בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי' signals that he is about to show that his own view has a good reason behind it, while theirs does not. The actual reason comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this?! Rejects a comparison as not valid.
Granted / it works well: introduces the side that has no difficulty.
According to me.

phrases.english: And I said to them: What is this (comparison)?
Granted, according to me,
since I say four cubits —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ אֲנָא: הַאי מַאי? בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה responds to the חכמים' counter-argument in Step 11 by denying that the two cases are truly alike.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: רבה claims his view and theirs are not comparable (the explanation continues on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The skewers paradox seems to apply equally to the four-טפחים and four-אמות views.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה is about to show that under four אמות the paradox does not truly arise (completed on the next amud).
